status.label: Reproduce cross-layout monitor reassociation
status.detail: Separate the supplied reopen jump from later HDR/display-change behavior and an unrelated multilayer-layout feature request.

next_action.label: Trace work-area identity and snap fallback
next_action.reason: History already includes layout IDs; adding another ID blindly would not establish a fix.

judgment.rationale: The original Explorer/layout-change/close/reopen sequence stops jumping when FancyZones is disabled. Follow-ups broaden the case to refresh-rate/HDR transitions and same zone indices in unrelated layouts; no concrete implementation establishes coverage.
evidence: The PowerToys 0.78 report supplies a numbered sequence and a FancyZones-disabled control.
One follow-up found a secondary monitor unexpectedly using the main monitor's layout; another describes display-change moves and asks separately for multilayer layouts.
FancyZones history lookups already use work-area identity and layout ID.

UpdateWorkAreas collects persisted zone-index properties, tries current-monitor history and then scans other work areas for matching saved zone sets; OnDisplayChange separately controls positional updates.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce reopen and display-change cases separately and trace target selection, preserving genuine unplug recovery while preventing unrelated-layout reassociation if confirmed.

fix_assessment.rationale: There is a concrete work-area/history reconciliation boundary to investigate; neither broad display tracking nor an external utility issue supplies a targeted fix.

proposed_fixes.title: Keep FancyZones snap history bound to the intended monitor/layout
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: after layout/display changes, old zone-index window properties and fallback history matching can select another work area. Existing layout-aware lookups are counterevidence against a simple missing-layout-ID claim; runtime target selection is still unconfirmed.
plan: Reproduce the original Explorer reopen case independently from refresh-rate/HDR work-area recreation, with distinct layouts on two monitors.
Trace the window's current zone property, source/target work-area IDs, layout IDs, saved history matches and each Snap decision.
If stale provenance or multiple fallback matches are confirmed, select one valid intended target deterministically and avoid reusing bare zone indices across unrelated layouts.
Retain deliberate movement options and genuine unplug/replug recovery; do not disable all display-change repositioning as a workaround.
Add regressions for changed layouts, same-index/different-layout histories, no-layout secondary monitors and display-transition option controls.
verification: Explorer reopens on the intended monitor after changing layout and does not immediately jump to the secondary.
HDR/refresh-rate changes do not map old zone indices into unrelated layouts.
Actual monitor removal still recovers windows correctly and opt-in movement settings retain their meaning.

confidence.rationale: The public sequence and inspected current-monitor/fallback history branches identify a plausible association boundary. No trace yet establishes which branch causes the original reopen jump, and the later display case may differ.

issue_context.summary: FancyZones can move a reopened window to the wrong monitor after changing layouts; later comments describe related display-change reassociation and a separate feature request.
known_information: The initial report includes a FancyZones-disabled control and affected Explorer/Telegram examples.
Follow-ups describe refresh-rate/HDR changes and layout confusion on a secondary monitor.
Existing history matching already uses work-area and layout identifiers.
The source also restores zone-index-tagged windows through a cross-work-area fallback.
inferences: A stale or ambiguous association is plausible, but the original reopen path and later display-change path must not be treated as one proven defect.
issue_context.analysis: The report is sufficient for maintainer reproduction. A blind proposal to add layout IDs duplicates existing safeguards and overlooks fallback target selection; the multilayer-layout feature request is outside this bug fix.
initial_investigation: Read the full report, both comments and obvious linked display-change work.
Inspected layout-aware history lookups and OnDisplayChange options.
Traced UpdateWorkAreas through work-area recreation, zone-index property collection, current-monitor matching and cross-work-area fallback snapping.

actions.label: Review monitor/layout provenance plan
actions.description: Approve the bounded target-selection investigation, not a new multilayer layout feature.

actions.label: Reproduce reopen and display-change monitor jumps

prerequisites: Use two monitors with distinct layouts and a current build; back up FancyZones settings.
Prepare an instrumented build logging non-sensitive work-area/layout IDs, zone sets and chosen Snap target.
Use HDR or refresh-rate transitions only where supported and keep them separate from the basic reopen test.
steps: Zone Explorer on the primary, switch its layout, close and reopen Explorer; compare with FancyZones disabled.
Repeat with a different secondary layout and with no secondary layout; inspect saved history and actual target.
With an open zoned window, change refresh rate or HDR and repeat with display-change movement off and on.
Create same-zone-index histories in distinct layouts and trace every fallback match; separately unplug/replug a monitor as a recovery control.
reproduce.expected_result: Windows retain the intended monitor/layout association, while deliberate display-movement and true unplug recovery continue to work.
reproduce.setup_prompt: Prepare two clearly distinct layouts that share a zone index but not a layout ID. Run reopen and HDR/refresh-rate experiments as separate cases and record selected work-area targets rather than personal window content.
